body:
GitHub issue #365. This is #326 F4 ("revision binds tree not diff", ADR-0007) biting
repeatedly in practice. NOT the same as #355 (F1, truncation).

## Problem

`resolveRevision` (`packages/core/lib/revision.mjs`) hashes EVERY tracked and untracked file
minus `ignorePaths`. An attestation therefore binds to the whole worktree, not to the change
that was reviewed. Any advance of `main` invalidates an attestation for a change that has not
moved.

## Evidence (#362, 2026-07-27)

1. Attestation recorded and green for revision `git-worktree:71c7050a...`.
2. Branch rebased onto newer main, picking up ONE commit — #361 (Copilot integration docs,
   marketing facts, `plugins/adlc-herdr/package.json`). No interaction with the reviewed code.
3. Revision moved to `a42b9cf8...`; the `gate` check went red.
4. The reviewed change was BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical — verified mechanically: the cumulative
   diff of the three changed files against the merge-base was 12950 bytes before and after the
   rebase, `diff` reporting no difference.

A fully reviewed, unchanged change was rejected because someone merged documentation. Per the
prior handoff notes, main advanced ~4 times during #314, invalidating the attestation each time.

## Why this matters beyond the annoyance

The cost is what the treadmill TEACHES. Facing a red gate on an unchanged, already-reviewed
diff, the tempting moves are (a) re-record without re-reviewing, making the attestation a
rubber stamp, or (b) drop the attestation and admin-override. The previous handoff document
recommended (b) as standard practice: "Unless you can rebase+re-record+merge within one quiet
window, just drop the attestation and admin-override." Both hollow out the gate — the same
erosion pattern as the session-lifetime ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS in #162/#204. A mechanism whose
correct use is impractical trains people out of using it correctly.

## Candidate designs (DECISION REQUIRED before build)

A. Bind to `(base_sha, diff_hash)`. A rebase onto a new base is then explicitly not covered
   (correct), but the common case is handled by B.
B. Explicit rebase re-attestation: a first-class operation that PROVES the diff is byte-
   identical, records the new base, and carries the prior verdict forward with an auditable
   link. Does not pretend a human re-reviewed.
C. Narrow the revision hash to exclude paths outside the diff. Simplest, weakest — it stops
   binding the context the change sits in, which is part of what makes review meaningful.

Author's lean: A+B. C alone trades one soundness problem for another.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An attestation for an UNCHANGED diff survives an unrelated advance of main, OR a documented
   auditable re-attestation path exists that does not require a fresh human review of an
   unchanged diff. Verify: a test rebases a fixture branch onto a new base that touches only
   unrelated files and asserts the attestation still satisfies the gate (or that the
   re-attestation path succeeds and records the carried-forward link).
2. A rebase that DOES change the diff still invalidates the attestation. Verify: a sibling
   test mutates one reviewed line and asserts the gate fails — this is the no-blanket-
   weakening guard and must be RED if criterion 1's mechanism is over-broad.
3. A same-provider or missing attestation still fails, and the distinct-provider requirement
   is unchanged. Verify: existing cross-model tests still pass unmodified.
4. ADR-0007's F4 entry is updated with the chosen resolution and its residual limits.
5. Full suite plus preflight green.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken the distinct-provider or signature requirements; this ticket changes WHAT the
  attestation binds to, nothing else.
- Any carry-forward path must be auditable — it must be possible to see, from the ledger
  alone, that a verdict was carried forward rather than freshly reviewed, and which prior
  verdict it came from.
- Touches `packages/core/` and `packages/prosecute/` — trust-root tier, so P5 is cross-model
  gated.

## Note on sequencing

The design decision (A / B / C) is a human call and gates the build. Do not implement before
it is made.
title: Cross-model attestation binds the whole worktree, not the reviewed diff — unrelated main activity invalidates a reviewed change (#326 F4)
